**Data.** EU-ForDAM (`value1`, 2000–2022, 16 countries, 77 NUTS units) and the NUTS forest appendix (area and growing stock of spruce, pine, fir, oak, all conifers, all broadleaves). Reported damage only, no gap-filling. 0 = recorded, no damage; missing = left out.

**Units.** Borers = m³ of trees killed; defoliators = ha defoliated (not necessarily killed). The two are never added together.

**Guild vs species.** Guild graphs add up all codes of the guild (aggregate codes included). Species graphs show individual species only. Borers and defoliators are always shown on separate graphs.

**Host tree.** The host tree in the data file; insects feeding on several trees get the wider group (e.g. *L. monacha* spruce and pine, *L. dispar* broadleaves, *Melolontha* all forest). Larch, birch, elm and poplar are not separate in the forest appendix, so those species are divided by all conifers / all broadleaves. Check: damage never exceeds the host in any region and year (except Vienna, where the appendix gives 0 spruce but small spruce bark-beetle damage is reported).

## 5. Usable pairs as time series

The 28 usable pairs from the correlation metrics (strong link that holds in every country checked), shown year by year. Only region-years where both insects are recorded; each region's series compared with its own normal (0 = normal year, +1 = one standard deviation worse), then averaged over the regions. Lines moving together = the correlation r.

Pairs are grouped by what the two insects are (the paper's level-1 groups): both borers on gymnosperms; a borer on gymnosperms with a borer on angiosperms; both borers on angiosperms; both defoliators on gymnosperms; a borer with a defoliator. Each panel names both insects with their guild and host tree.

## 6. Bringing in more countries

Species pairs can only be tested where both insects are reported, mostly Germany, Czechia, Poland and Lithuania (Finland, Sweden and Switzerland report only *I. typographus*). Two ways to use more countries:

**(1) The paper's groups.** Group value = sum of all member codes in a region-year (aggregates included), so countries reporting few insects still contribute. Correlation per country and pooled.

![](../outputs/figures/final/6_more_countries/6a_level1_r_per_country.png)

![](../outputs/figures/final/6_more_countries/6b_level2_r_per_country.png)

![](../outputs/figures/final/6_more_countries/6c_level1_time_series.png)

![](../outputs/figures/final/6_more_countries/6d_level2_time_series.png)

**(2) Europe-wide yearly totals (the 2025 paper's approach).** For each insect or group, the sum over every reporting region of every country each year, log(1 + x), correlated over the 23 years.

![](../outputs/figures/final/6_more_countries/6e_level1_europe_totals.png)

![](../outputs/figures/final/6_more_countries/6f_usable_pairs_europe_totals.png)

![](../outputs/figures/final/6_more_countries/6g_usable_pairs_within_vs_europe.png)

## Things to keep in mind

- Germany carries 52% of all borer damage and Poland 50% of all defoliation; most countries start reporting in 2003 (Austria 2002, Poland 2003, Finland 2012).
- Some dips come from how values were recorded, not from the insects: Bavaria *I. typographus* 2007 (6,000 m³) and 2009 (3,633 m³) next to millions in other years, and 0 in 2015; Hesse and Saxony-Anhalt report 0 for every insect from 2006–2007 on. These are listed in `outputs/tables/CHECK_suspicious_values_for_data_providers.csv`.
- Defoliated hectares are hectare-years: the same stand can count in several years and under several species.
- Averages hide outbreaks: e.g. *L. dispar* averages about 105,000 ha a year but a typical year is about 29,000 ha.
- In the defoliator guild share graphs *Melolontha* is left out (it feeds in all forest, not only broadleaves); it is included in the total-damage graphs.
- Bulgaria and Lithuania single-species growing stocks in the forest appendix are read as 1,000 m³ (otherwise far below their reported damage).

---

## 7. Summary of the usable pairs (with the multiple-testing check)

786 pairs could be measured. Testing that many, about 39 would look "sure" by luck alone. The false discovery rate (FDR, Benjamini-Hochberg) correction allows for this: after it, 150 links stay sure, and **all 28 usable pairs stay sure** (q < 0.05). For 21 of them the regional part is sure on its own as well. p-values come from the same region bootstrap as the 95% ranges (whole regions resampled, 9,999 draws).

![](../outputs/figures/final/CM_usable_pairs_summary_table.png)

Table: `outputs/tables/CM_usable_pairs_summary.csv`; every pair with p and q: `outputs/tables/CM_pairs_fdr.csv`.
